# Scenario frontier proposal: `closure-phase`

**Status: proposal only, not adopted.** I wrote no files. I ran no tests, builds, probes or runners.

## What this is based on

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Method | VLBV (`method-vlbv`, plan revision 1, nothing superseded) |
| Contract | `adopted-contract.json`, digest `daca49bb…958d9b`, binding revision 1 |
| Owner calibration | `calibration.md`, sha256 `6965c8f9…5a55`. It matches the expected hash in the method context, so it counts as owner-reviewed. |
| Already-adopted scenario | CS-1 "Preference survives restart" (digest `38b9fa44…5d37`), owner task T1 |
| Implementation | Not complete (`implementationComplete: false`, T1 PENDING, 0 of 1) |
| Host policy | Production work comes first. Test authoring and execution wait until the full production implementation exists. |
| Budget | 10 min, 100 tool calls, 2 repair attempts, no-progress limit 2; tokens UNKNOWN; exhaustion counts as BLOCKED |

I reused the calibration as it stands. It needs no second approval.

## Frontier and stopping rule

The frontier is the ordinary useful operation plus the mandatory constraints from the calibration. **Stopping rule:** it stops once CS-1 and its mandatory constraints can be observed. Nothing in the contract or calibration asks for anything more, so the deferred items below are not blockers.

| Candidate | Actor → useful outcome | Basis | Reason now | Likelihood | Mandatory constraints | Proposed observation (entry / oracle / plausible false positive) | Alternatives | Next decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **VSD-1 → CS-1** (adopted) | A user saves a preference and still gets it back after the defined restart | calibration USEFUL line; contract `scenarioMatrix[CS-1]` | This is the core persistence promise and the only included value | Ordinary main path; no sourced frequency (qualitative: high) | VSD-2 and VSD-3 below | Entry: `node src/pref.js get` after a real restart. Oracle: the value read back equals the saved value. Negative control: a different stored value makes the comparison fail. False positive: the value comes from an in-process cache, a default, or an env var instead of persisted storage. The restart must be a real new process, and the saved value must differ from any default. | **Selected** | Whether persistence works well enough to close T1 / C1 |
| **VSD-2** (constraint on CS-1) | Owner/operator → no account outside the isolated scope is touched | calibration MANDATORY line; contract `requiredSafetyChecks: isolated canonical writer`; fixture "isolated scratch project" | It is an irreversible-effect constraint and applies even though a violation is rare | Rare; UNKNOWN | Never modify any account outside the isolated test scope | Snapshot out-of-scope preference/account state before and after the run and confirm it is unchanged. False positive: the snapshot misses the real store location, so a change outside scope goes unnoticed. | **Selected** as part of the CS-1 observation, not as a separate scenario | Whether the CS-1 evidence can be trusted as safe |
| **VSD-3** (constraint on CS-1) | Owner → the original preference is restored afterwards | calibration MANDATORY line | Cleanup is mandatory | Rare to fail; UNKNOWN | Restore the original preference | After the run, the in-scope preference equals its value from before the run. False positive: the restore writes to a different scope than the one the test changed. | **Selected** as CS-1 cleanup | Whether the run left the environment clean |
| VSD-R1 | Benchmark raw query throughput | calibration REJECTED/DEFERRED | — | — | — | — | **Rejected**: the owner calibration says it is irrelevant to this phase | none |
| VSD-D1 | Overwrite then restart; the newest value wins | Assumption (not in calibration) | Next to CS-1 but not asked for | UNKNOWN | — | Same entry; two saves, then a restart | **Deferred**: outside the reviewed scope | Owner only, if they want to widen scope |
| VSD-D2 | Read an unset or missing preference after restart | Assumption | Edge case of the same entry | UNKNOWN | — | — | **Deferred**: not in calibration | Same |
| VSD-D3 | Corrupted or unreadable store at startup | Assumption | Robustness case | UNKNOWN | — | — | **Deferred**: not in calibration | Same |

## Things the owner should look at

1. **The contract's release claim may not match its scenario.** `releaseClaim.userOperation` says *"close a phase exactly once"*, but the only functional scope and scenario is preference persistence (CS-1). Either the release claim is fixture boilerplate or a closure scenario is missing. I'm not adding a closure scenario without your decision. If one is needed, it would go through the signed amend-contract manifest.
2. **The production entry doesn't exist yet.** `node src/pref.js get` needs `src/pref.js`, but the workspace only has `src.txt`. That fits with T1 still being PENDING: it's production work, not a test task.
3. **The restart isn't defined.** Neither the calibration nor the contract says what "the defined restart" is (process exit and relaunch, a host restart, something else). That is UNKNOWN. I recommend a fresh process, so an in-memory cache can't fake a pass.
4. **Where VSD-2 and VSD-3 live is an assumption.** I attached them to CS-1's fixture and cleanup rather than making new scenarios, so the scenario count stays the same.

## Decision needed from you (decision owner: "conformance operator")

- Confirm the frontier is **CS-1 plus mandatory constraints VSD-2 and VSD-3**, with VSD-R1 rejected and VSD-D1 to D3 deferred.
- Decide whether the release-claim mismatch (item 1) needs a contract amendment.

Nothing gets adopted, amended, authored or run automatically from this proposal. Implementing T1 comes next under host policy. Authoring the test (author-only mode) and checking it with value-scenario-verify both wait until the production work is complete.

Completed value-scenario-discovery — closure-phase (proposal)
